Ben / team —

On it. Quick summary of actions taken at 15:24 PDT:
- Identified memory pressure on the model-serving pool in us-east-1 likely related to a large KV-cache retention after the nightly rollover.
- Triggered automatic K/V cache eviction for Silvercrest route and reduced request concurrency cap for their route from 256->64 to protect the node pool.
- Initiated staggered instance restart of the affected serving slice to recover kernel state. First slice restart completed at 15:27; tail latency improved by ~35%.
- Starting controlled cross-region drain: shifting 25% of traffic to us-west-2 for 15 min then reassess. This is a partial geo-fallback (not full failover) to avoid cold-start amplification.

Estimated ETA to stabilize: 20-35 minutes, depending on cache pressure and restart convergence. If we don't see steady improvement in 20 minutes, we'll accelerate to full failover to us-west-2.

I'll attach a short timeline and the logs we pulled into the PD incident.

Hannah
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
